key_insight: The paper shows that weld penetration status can be predicted more reliably across different welding processes by using unsupervised domain adaptation instead of relying only on labeled source data. Its key idea is to reduce the performance drop caused by transferring a model from TIG welding to laser welding, where the underlying physics are very different.
problem_solved: Supervised weld-state classifiers often fail when deployed in a new welding process because of domain shift between source and target processes. This work addresses cross-process transfer from arc-based TIG welding to keyhole-based laser welding without requiring labels in the target domain.
method: Uses an unsupervised domain adaptation framework to transfer knowledge from a labeled source welding process to an unlabeled target process.
Integrates gradual source domain expansion (GSDE) to progressively broaden the source representation and improve cross-process robustness.
Targets weld penetration status classification under strong process-to-process differences in signal and physical mechanism.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this demonstrates a practical way to build models that generalize across industrial domains where labeled target data is scarce or unavailable. It is especially relevant for manufacturing AI, where process changes often break standard supervised models.

paper_title: A cross-process welding penetration status prediction algorithm based on unsupervised domain adaptation in laser and TIG welding
paper_authors: Sen Li, Haichao Cui, Chendong Shao, Yaqi Wang, Xinhua Tang
